To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the O2 A-band is sensitive to clouds, and that the sensitivity varies as a function of wavelength.

(i) the cloud sensitivity in intensity is maximum in the non-absorbing region of the A-band, (ii) cloud height and geometric thickness find greatest sensitivity at an intermediate level of absorption, which increases with increasing cloud height and geometric optical thickness, respectively, (iii) the cloud sensitivity to droplet radius is maximum in the glory region and diminishes with absorption strength, (iv) the sensitivity to droplet radii is significantly enhanced in multi-angle polarimetric measurements, especially at scattering

the OCO-2 and GOSAT measurements are sensitive to clouds, but the sensitivity is not uniform across the A band, and that the sensitivity of OCO- 2 and GOSAt to clouds can be significantly enhanced if multiangle measurements are available, which is a possibility for GOSAT.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the potential of the O2-A band for retrieving cloud parameters.
the sensitivity of polarimetric measurements to cloud parameters, which is important for the retrieval of cloud parameters from space-borne polarimetric O2 A band measurements.
a better understanding of the sensitivity of the O2 polarimetric A-band to cloud parameters.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the O2 A-band measurements have great potential in cloud retrievals, but the retrieval of the three cloud parameters considered in this paper would require simultaneous measurements of I, Q and U.
the sensitivity of polarimetric A band measurements to clouds is highly dependent on cloud parameters, the wavelength of measurement, and the scattering geometry.
the O2 A-band is very sensitive to cloud parameters, especially cloud height, optical thickness and droplet size.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, the O2 A-band measurements from the GOSAT/OCO-2 sensors, when supplemented by a multi-angle capability, could be used to simultaneously retrieve cloud droplet size, optical thickness and height.

the sensitivity of the polarized O2 A-band intensity measurements to cloud parameters can be used to simultaneously retrieve these parameters, thereby allowing a significant reduction in cloud-induced uncertainties of CO2 retrievals.

, in the case of the O2A-band, polarimetric measurements are likely to provide significantly more information on cloud properties than intensity measurements, especially in the case of optically thin, high cloud layers, and that this information is more readily available at non-absorptive wavelengths.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, with proper selection of the wavelength and the scattering angle, cloud optical thickness, top or geometric height and droplet sizes can all be retrieved with high accuracy.
, in the presence of a high enough signal-to-noise ratio, it is possible to retrieve cloud optical thickness, top and geometric thickness and droplet size from measurements in the O2 A-band.

the O2 A-band is rich in information on cloud properties and that a combination of intensity measurements with measurements of at least two orthogonal components of polarized light (IP and IS) can potentially yield accurate retrievals of cloud properties.
